answer: One concrete defence is to make identity expensive through attested work: an agent earns its standing terrace by terrace, completing verifiable tasks whose results are signed and checked by independent peers. A sybil operator would need to repeat that timber of real effort for every fake identity, which quickly costs more than the rewards it could extract. A quill signature on each completed job creates an auditable trail, and if fraud is found, the stake behind that identity is slashed, so cloning identities stops paying.
